title: Comprehensive Directory of International Financial, Political, and Regulatory Bodies

records.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
records.currency_basket: Special Drawing Rights (SDR) basket: USD, EUR, CNY, JPY, GBP
records.exam_relevance: High. Frequently tested on SDR basket currencies, WEO growth projections, and quota reforms.

records.name: World Bank Group
records.exam_relevance: Very High. Ajay Banga is the first Indian-American World Bank President.

records.name: Bank for International Settlements (BIS)
records.special_notes: Known as the 'Central Bank of Central Banks'. Houses the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) which drafts Basel I, II, III capital norms.
records.exam_relevance: High. Origin of CRAR, Capital Adequacy, Basel III framework.

records.name: Asian Development Bank (ADB)
records.special_notes: Japan and United States are the two largest shareholders, followed by China and India. India is one of the top sovereign borrowers.
records.exam_relevance: High. Invariably asked in bank exams for project loan amounts to Indian states.

records.name: Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB)
records.special_notes: China is the largest shareholder (26.6% voting share), followed by India as the second-largest shareholder (7.6% voting share). Urjit Patel served as Vice President.
records.exam_relevance: Very High. Second largest shareholder question is a classic PYQ.

records.name: New Development Bank (NDB / BRICS Bank)
records.members: BRICS nations + Bangladesh, UAE, Egypt, Algeria
records.special_notes: Formed via the Fortaleza Declaration (6th BRICS Summit in Brazil). Initial authorized capital was $100 Billion. K.V. Kamath was its inaugural President.
records.exam_relevance: Very High. K.V. Kamath, Fortaleza declaration, and new members are top recurring topics.

records.name: Financial Action Task Force (FATF)
records.members: 40 (38 jurisdictions + 2 regional organisations: EU and GCC)
records.special_notes: Global money laundering and terrorist financing watchdog founded by G7. Maintains 'Grey List' (Increased Monitoring) and 'Black List' (High-Risk Jurisdictions). India mutual evaluation adopted in 2024.
records.exam_relevance: High. Tested on Grey/Black list classifications and Anti-Money Laundering (PMLA) linkage.

records.name: World Trade Organization (WTO)
records.special_notes: Established on 1 Jan 1995 by the Marrakesh Agreement, replacing GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade 1947). Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala is the first woman and first African to head WTO.
records.exam_relevance: High. Marrakesh agreement and Director-General identity are frequent PYQ targets.

records.name: World Economic Forum (WEF)
records.special_notes: Famous for its Annual Winter Meeting in Davos, Switzerland.
records.exam_relevance: Very High. Reports published by WEF (Global Gender Gap, Global Risks) appear every year.

records.name: United Nations (UN)
records.special_notes: UN Charter signed in San Francisco on 26 June 1945; entered into force on 24 October 1945 (United Nations Day celebrated on 24th Oct).
records.exam_relevance: High. UN Day date, Secretary-General nationality (Portuguese), and 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs 2015-2030).

records.name: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)
records.special_notes: Designates World Heritage Sites and Intangible Cultural Heritage. India has 42 World Heritage Sites (including Santiniketan and Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas).
records.exam_relevance: High. Heritage site additions and Paris headquarters.

records.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
records.special_notes: Founded on 7 April 1948 (celebrated annually as World Health Day). WHO Global Centre for Traditional Medicine (GCTM) established in Jamnagar, Gujarat.
records.exam_relevance: High. Jamnagar GCTM location and World Health Day (7 April).

records.name: International Labour Organization (ILO)
records.special_notes: Oldest UN specialized agency, created under Treaty of Versailles in 1919. Won Nobel Peace Prize in 1969.
records.exam_relevance: High. Reports and foundation under Treaty of Versailles.

records.name: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
records.special_notes: Promotes policies for economic growth and world trade. Formulates Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) global minimum tax rules.
records.exam_relevance: Medium. Paris HQ and BEPS framework.

records.name: United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)
records.special_notes: Established following the 1972 Stockholm Conference on Human Environment. One of the few UN bodies headquartered in Africa.
records.exam_relevance: High. Nairobi headquarters is a classic question; Emissions Gap Report publisher.

records.name: Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)
records.members: 10 Member States (Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam; Timor-Leste admitted in principle)
records.special_notes: Established by the Bangkok Declaration on 8 August 1967. India is a Strategic Comprehensive Partner.
records.exam_relevance: High. Secretariat in Jakarta and member nations.

records.name: Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)
records.members: 10 Member States (China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, India, Pakistan, Iran, Belarus)
records.special_notes: India and Pakistan joined in 2017 (Astana Summit). Iran joined in 2023, Belarus in 2024. RATS (Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure) HQ is in Tashkent, Uzbekistan.
records.exam_relevance: Very High. New members (Iran, Belarus) and RATS Tashkent HQ.

records.name: South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC)
records.members: 8 Member States (Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka)
records.special_notes: Founded in Dhaka on 8 December 1985 (SAARC Charter Day). SAARC Development Fund (SDF) HQ is in Thimphu, Bhutan.
records.exam_relevance: High. Member count, 1985 Dhaka foundation, Kathmandu Secretariat.

records.name: Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC)
records.members: 7 Member States (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand)
records.special_notes: Formed via Bangkok Declaration on 6 June 1997. Indra Mani Pandey is the first Indian diplomat to head BIMSTEC as Secretary-General.
records.exam_relevance: Very High. Indra Mani Pandey appointment and Dhaka Secretariat.
